content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑sugar chocolate milk is a beverage made from whole cow’s milk, enriched with cocoa butter and natural flavorings. The lower sugar content makes it more suitable for people monitoring glucose levels while preserving the classic chocolate taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The reduced sugar is achieved by using stevia and erythritol, which do not raise blood glucose.
Cocoa butter retains beneficial polyphenols known for antioxidant properties.
The product is certified by NFS (National Food Standards), guaranteeing compliance with high food quality standards.
Chocolate milk is often used in sports nutrition as a quick source of carbs and protein after workouts.
Compared with regular chocolate milk, this version has lower calories per serving.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Milk provides an excellent source of calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Each serving delivers about 8 g of protein, aiding muscle recovery.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: Reduced sugar and sweet‑eners result in a milder effect on blood sugar levels.

items.title: Antioxidants from cocoa
items.content: Cocoa polyphenols help combat free radicals and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Milk supplies vitamin B2 (riboflavin) and vitamin B12, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance should choose lactose‑free versions or alternative drinks.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey can trigger reactions even in small amounts.

items.title: Sweet‑ener side effects
items.content: Erythritol and stevia may cause mild gastrointestinal discomfort when consumed in large quantities.

items.title: Caloric content
items.content: Although sugar is reduced, the drink still contains calories, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reduced‑sugar chocolate milk can be enjoyed chilled as a refreshing drink, added to smoothies, used in desserts, or consumed as a post‑workout recovery beverage.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 1 °C–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5 days. Do not freeze, as it may alter the texture.

content.title: About
content.content: Cooked lotus root (Nelumbo nucifera) is the edible rhizome of the lotus plant. After cooking it retains a crisp texture and a mildly sweet, nutty flavor. In Asian cuisines it is used in soups, salads, stir‑fries, and as a side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lotus root has a distinctive pattern of holes that looks like a star when sliced.
In Chinese and Japanese cooking it is often sliced thin and quickly stir‑fried.
The lotus is a symbol of purity and rebirth in Buddhism and Taoism.
Raw lotus root can be slightly bitter; cooking removes the bitterness.
Traditional Chinese medicine uses lotus root to aid digestion and strengthen the lungs.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports healthy digestion, helps maintain satiety, and regulates blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts the immune system and provides antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain fluid balance and normal blood pressure.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Cooked lotus root is low in calories, making it a good choice for weight‑managed diets.

items.title: Provides vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to lotus, such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Water‑borne contamination
items.content: Lotus grows in stagnant water, so thorough washing and proper cooking are essential to avoid microbial contamination.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: High oxalate levels may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked lotus root can be sliced thin and added to salads, soups, stews, or stir‑fries. It is also used in sushi rolls and as a rice side dish. Before cooking, peel the outer skin and rinse well.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked lotus root in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. Fresh roots keep best in a cool, humid environment and should be used within a week.

content.title: About
content.content: Beef soup is a classic dish made from beef, vegetables, and broth. It has a rich meaty flavor, aromatic spices, and a warming effect. Common variations include potatoes, carrots, onions, celery, and noodles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef soup is one of the oldest dishes mentioned in ancient culinary texts.
Different countries have their own versions: French "bouillon de boeuf", Japanese "gyūniku suupu", and American "beef noodle soup".
Traditionally, beef is simmered for several hours to extract maximum gelatin and flavor.
Beef broth is rich in collagen, which turns into jelly when cooled.
Some cultures add sauerkraut or fermented beans to the soup for extra depth.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef supplies easily absorbed heme iron, important for blood formation.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: B‑vitamins in beef help convert food into energy.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: A warm broth helps maintain fluid balance, especially in cold weather.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Large portions can raise cholesterol; choose lean cuts when possible.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Broth can be salty; consider reducing added salt.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Rare, but possible for individuals with meat allergies.

items.title: Contamination
items.content: Undercooked meat may harbor harmful bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, garnish with fresh herbs, lemon juice, or hot sauce to taste. Pair with bread, croutons, or rice for a complete meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the soup to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for up to 2 months. Reheat to a rolling boil before serving.
